package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions contain a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2024-11639) that allows remote attackers to gain administrative privileges without authentication, enabling full compromise of the appliance. This vulnerability undermines the core security boundary of the device, exposing sensitive configuration and data to unauthorized parties.

execution_context.trigger: When a network request is made to the CSA administrative web interface
execution_context.file_location: Proprietary web application authentication handler (exact file not disclosed in report)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (proprietary, not disclosed in report); described as an alternate code path or logic flaw that bypasses normal authentication checks, allowing direct access to administrative functions.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely C/C++ or proprietary web scripting language used by Ivanti CSA)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving a network request to the administrative interface, the authentication handler processes the request using an alternate code path that skips credential verification, directly granting administrative session privileges to the requester, resulting in unauthorized access to all administrative functions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code enables unauthenticated users to access privileged administrative functions, which is a severe violation of security best practices and exposes the system to full compromise by remote attackers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard authentication handlers require valid credentials and session validation before granting administrative access; this vulnerability allows bypassing all authentication and authorization checks, directly violating the expected security model.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Alternate authentication paths may exist for internal diagnostics or support, but such mechanisms must be strictly access-controlled and never exposed to unauthenticated remote users. Exposure of such a path to the public interface is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Presence of an authentication bypass in the administrative interface
Alternate or undocumented code path that omits credential checks
Successful administrative actions performed without prior authentication
Network requests to admin endpoints resulting in privilege escalation without valid session tokens

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specifically crafted network request to the CSA administrative interface, exploiting the alternate authentication bypass path to circumvent credential checks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthenticated administrative privileges on the appliance.

attack_chain.action: With administrative access, the attacker modifies configurations, exfiltrates sensitive data, or deploys additional malware, leveraging full control over the appliance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Complete compromise of the appliance and potential lateral movement within the network.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated access attempts to administrative endpoints resulting in successful sessions
Network requests to CSA admin interfaces lacking valid session tokens or authentication headers
Configuration changes or administrative actions performed by unknown or unauthenticated users
Unexpected privilege escalation events originating from external or untrusted IP addresses
file_indicators: No specific file indicators available (vulnerability resides in proprietary authentication logic not exposed to file system monitoring)
network_indicators: Unusual or unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to CSA administrative web interface endpoints
Access attempts to /admin or similar privileged URLs from external or untrusted IP addresses
Absence of authentication headers or session tokens in requests that result in administrative access
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor logs for successful access to administrative endpoints without corresponding authentication events. Set up alerts for network requests to CSA admin interfaces that lack valid session tokens or authentication headers, especially from external or untrusted sources. Correlate configuration changes or privilege escalations with user authentication records to identify actions performed by unauthenticated or unknown users. Review for any administrative actions initiated from IP addresses not associated with legitimate administrators.
